chunks: Symmetrical power bridge pros and cons. The question: What are the pros and cons of a symmetrical power bridge?
A symmetrical bridge uses two identical transistors in the half bridge. That is simple and flexible, and it lets the bridge run in both directions.
In a buck, though, the two transistors do different jobs and spend different amounts of time on, so identical parts waste some efficiency unless the duty cycle is near 50 percent.
Imagine two workers of the same size sharing a shift. One works 10 percent of the day and the other works 90 percent.
The second one gets exhausted while the first one is mostly idle. A smarter split gives the busy job to the stronger worker. Here "stronger" means a lower resistance.
The symmetrical half bridge. Same device, same drive, same ratings on both sides. At D equals 0. 1 the high side conducts only 10% of the time.
Half bridge: two transistors in a stack with the switch node between them. Conduction loss: heat wasted as I squared R while a transistor is on.
Duty cycle ( D ): the fraction of time the top transistor is on ("What is duty cycle"). Bidirectional: able to move power either way, as buck or boost.
Body diode: the built-in diode inside a MOSFET.
Make both transistors 10 milliohms, with 2 amps flowing and D equals 0. 1 (about 12 volts to 1. 2 volts). The top one conducts 10 percent of the time and loses 2 squared times 0.
01 times 0. 1 equals 4 milliwatts. The bottom one conducts 90 percent and loses 2 squared times 0. 01 times 0. 9 equals 36 milliwatts. That is the whole idea.
"I'd take symmetrical to mean two identical FETs in the half bridge.
Pros: one part number, identical drive and timing, and bidirectional capability, so it's good near 50% duty and for inverters or bidirectional converters.
Con: in a buck the high side conducts D and hard-switches while the low side conducts 1-D with near-zero-voltage switching, so equal sizing wastes silicon at small duty.
For fixed area the optimal conductance ratio is square root of D over (1-D) , which for D equals 0. 1 saves about 20% of conduction loss."
